questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A bakery throws away 10 unsold loaves of bread every evening. Which statement best describes the opportunity cost of this waste?

choices.text: The other goods the flour, energy, and work in the bread could have produced
The rent the bakery pays for its shop, which is due whether or not bread is wasted
The weekly fee the bakery pays to have its garbage collected
The money the bakery expects to earn from tomorrow's fresh bread

questions.prompt: Stores in a town hand out plastic bags at no charge. Economists predict that shoppers will use more bags than the socially efficient number. Which statement best explains this prediction?

choices.text: The social cost of a plastic bag falls to zero once the bag has been made.
Shoppers pay $0, which is less than the full cost of the bag to society.
Producing each plastic bag is very expensive for the store that hands it out.
Plastic bags are a necessity, so people need many of them for daily life.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Making one disposable takeout container costs 30 cents, and after it is used, disposal and environmental damage cost society another 45 cents (assumed values). What is the social cost of one container, in cents? (Enter a number only.)
Which statement best describes a deposit-return system for disposable cups (you get money back when you return the cup)?

choices.text: Refunds lower the price of cups, so consumers end up buying fewer cups overall.
It mainly provides information, so behavior tends to change little.
Refunds raise return and recycling rates, but return sites and upkeep cost money.
It raises collection, but the deposit is a permanent extra cost even for returners.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A reusable lunch container costs $9. Each time you use it instead of a disposable container, you avoid a 25-cent disposable-container charge, but washing it uses about 10 cents of water, soap, and energy. How many uses does it take for the reusable container to earn back its price? (Enter a number only.)
